test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 29 Aug 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following metals are more reactive than hydrogen?

Mg, Zn, Hg, Ag, Sn, Pb, Au, Fe, Na

options.text: Mg, Zn, Sn, Pb, Au, Na
Mg, Zn, Sn, Pb, Fe, Na
Mg, Zn, Hg, Pb, Fe, Na
Mg, Zn, Ag, Pb, Fe, Na

solution:
The correct answer is __**Mg, Zn, Sn, Pb, Fe, Na**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 2** includes the metals Mg, Zn, Sn, Pb, Fe, Na, which are all more reactive than hydrogen.
 
• According to the reactivity series of metals, these metals are positioned above hydrogen, indicating higher reactivity.
 
• Metals like Hg, Ag, and Au, which are not included in Option 2, are less reactive than hydrogen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **reactivity series** is a list of metals arranged in order of their reactivity from highest to lowest.
 
• Metals at the top of the series, such as Na (sodium) and Mg (magnesium), react more vigorously with water and acids compared to those lower in the series.
 
• Hydrogen is included in the reactivity series for comparison, even though it is a non-metal.
 
• Metals above hydrogen in the series can displace hydrogen from acids, whereas metals below hydrogen cannot.
